title: City police to help probe man's death
article: After his arrest, \[Paul Alphonse\] was taken to the Williams Lake RCMP detachment. More than four hours later, he complained of chest pains and was taken to the hospital. He remained in hospital until his death.

Even though Alphonse died in hospital, police are treating the matter as an in-custody death, as Alphonse was under lawful arrest at the time. An autopsy will be performed to determine the cause of death.
RCMP serious crime investigators from Kamloops and Prince George will investigate the death of a Williams Lake man in police custody.
Paul Alphonse, 67, died Tuesday in hospital Tuesday. He had been arrested in Williams Lake seven days previous for being drunk in a public place.

After his arrest, Alphonse was taken to the Williams Lake RCMP detachment. More than four hours later, he complained of chest pains and was taken to the hospital. He remained in hospital until his death.
The investigating team will also look at reports that Alphonse was the victim of excessive force during the course of the initial arrest.

The patrol officer who made the arrest remains on active duty pending the result of the investigation. Senior RCMP officers from the Williams Lake detachment are working with officials from the Williams lake Indian Band, police spokesman said.
The arresting officer's name was not released.
It's RCMP policy to turn investigations like this over to RCMP members from outside the detachment, the spokesman said.
